question: The hairy cell leukemia (hairy cell leukemia) presents as characteristic clinical-biological features:

options.opa: Lymphocytosis in peripheral blood greater than 50,000 lymphocytes / microL.
options.opc: Exfoliative generalized erythroderma, plaques and skin tumors.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Hairy cell leukemia" -> "characteristic lymphocytosis" -> "peripheral blood lymphocyte count > 50,000 / microL" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Hairy cell leukemia" -> "involvement of T lymphoid line" -> "presence of T lymphoid markers" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Hairy cell leukemia" -> "uncommon skin manifestations" -> "exfoliative generalized erythroderma" -> "plaques and skin tumors" -> "less typical" -> 60%
analysis: Hairy cell leukemia is characterized by pancytopenia and splenomegaly, which are common findings in this condition. Lymphocytosis is not typically greater than 50,000 lymphocytes/microL, and T lymphoid line markers are not specific to hairy cell leukemia. Exfoliative generalized erythroderma is not a feature of this leukemia. Therefore, the most accurate option is that hairy cell leukemia presents with pancytopenia and splenomegaly.
